findings.text: Freeze operation selects a surviving processor and powers down every other online processor toward the offline state while recording successes in a dedicated mask; thaw operation powers back up exactly the recorded set toward the online state and then clears the mask. Freeze accepts an explicit survivor or an automatic choice when given minus one, falling back to the first online processor with a preference for timer housekeeping. Both operations serialize against concurrent hotplug changes and report failures to the caller.

Mask lifecycle invariant: the frozen set starts empty for each freeze attempt, gains a member only after that processor was successfully taken down, is left untouched by thaw when empty, and is emptied after thaw finishes bringing members up. Iteration during freeze proceeds from high identifiers downward skipping offline and survivor processors, while thaw iterates over the recorded set in identifier order.

Freeze holds the processor maps update guard for its whole duration and increments the hotplug disabled nesting count even when it fails, requiring callers to run the thaw side when freeze reports an error to restore balance. Thaw holds the same guard, reenables hotplug use before checking the mask, and releases the guard afterwards. Power management prepare and post phases likewise disable and reenable hotplug around suspend and hibernation.
Early initialization allocates the frozen mask as a zeroed processor mask and reports out of memory if allocation fails. This must run before any freeze or thaw use.

Freeze aborts promptly if a system wakeup is pending, leaving already frozen processors recorded and returning busy. On full success it asserts that at most one processor remains online; otherwise it logs an error about incomplete shutdown. Partial failures leave the system with a mixture of online and newly offlined processors plus disabled hotplug until thaw runs.

Power notifier entry handles four actions: suspend prepare and hibernation prepare disable processor hotplug, while post suspend and post hibernation reenable it; all other actions are ignored as not handled. Registration occurs during early init with a priority chosen to run before platform boot processor handling to avoid races.
Global integer identifies the boot processor. Fragments show only its declaration, not how it is assigned or consumed.

Central hotplug table defines an ordered progression from a fully offline state through control processor preparation work, application processor bringup and synchronization, dying and online stages, optional split kick and bringup phases, teardown and scheduler draining, per subsystem online handling, scheduler activation, and a final fully online state, with a reserved gap for dynamically registered states. Each entry carries a human readable label, optional single startup and teardown handlers, and flags indicating whether the step may serve as a stable target and whether it supports multiple instances. Build options select single phase versus split bringup and include symmetric multiprocessing only stages.

State identifier validation accepts only values strictly between the offline and online boundaries; boundary values and anything outside are rejected as invalid. This check gates dynamic registration, setup and removal paths.

Dynamic allocation scans the application online dynamic range or the boot preparation dynamic range for the first entry without a label and returns its index, warning and reporting no space when full and rejecting any other base as invalid. Installation stores startup and teardown handlers plus label and multi instance flag and initializes the instance list; installing onto an already named entry is rejected as busy. Clearing is done by installing a null label, with special handling so that clearing does not accidentally allocate a fresh dynamic slot and leave old handlers dangling. Retrieval of the teardown handler is a simple lookup by state.

State table mutations and per processor invocations are serialized by a dedicated state mutex, while callers must already hold the processors read guard or the locked variants assert it; public wrappers acquire and release that read guard around the locked implementation. Removal and instance paths hold both guards while iterating present processors and touching instance lists.

Single step invocation looks up the step for the requested state and returns success immediately when no work exists for the requested direction. Symmetric multiprocessing builds dispatch application processor states through an application path and other states through a control path; other builds run atomic states under an interrupt saved guard and warn once if they fail. Any failure during teardown is treated as fatal.

Rollback after a failed multi processor install walks present processors in order up to but not including the failed one and invokes the teardown side of the same state for each processor whose current state had already reached or passed it. Setup failure additionally clears the just installed callbacks when a teardown handler was supplied.

Setup installs callbacks for a state and optionally runs startup immediately on every present processor whose current state is at or beyond it. Instance addition requires a multi instance state and optionally runs the multi startup for qualifying processors before linking the new node. Instance removal optionally runs multi teardown for qualifying processors before unlinking. Full state removal warns if multi instance entries still have linked instances and otherwise optionally runs teardown for qualifying processors before clearing. Dynamic base requests return the allocated concrete state on success.

Threading control disables by walking online processors under the maps guard, skipping primary threads and optionally skipping allowed threads when reducing counts, taking others down to offline and marking their devices offline; it updates the stored control value only on full success. Enabling sets the control value first, then walks present processors skipping online members, members on offline nodes, disallowed threads and members on offline cores, bringing the rest up to online and marking their devices online.

Device state helpers fetch the processor device, update its offline flag, and notify user space with an offline or online event. They are used by threading control because the maps guard is already held and the normal device offline path cannot be entered.

Per processor hotplug group exposes three decimal attributes for current state, desired target and injected failure state; a top level hotplug group exposes a states listing that prints each named state index with its label. Group name in both cases is hotplug.

Target attribute shows the desired state and stores a new target by parsing decimal input, rejecting out of range values and, depending on build configuration, either allowing any state between offline and online or only the two endpoints. It takes the device hotplug sysfs guard, rejects unnamed or non stoppable targets, then moves the processor up or down toward the target or repairs a mismatched target field when already there, returning the input length on success.

Failure injection attribute shows the configured failing state and stores a new value by parsing decimal input. A dedicated invalid value clears injection. Other values must lie within offline to online inclusive, must not select atomic starting or dying states, must not select states at or below bringup when the processor is currently beyond bringup, and must refer to a state that actually has handlers; otherwise the request is rejected.
States listing holds the state mutex while scanning from offline through online inclusive and emitting only entries that have a label, each as an index plus label line.
Thread count validation accepts one through the maximum inclusive when dynamic counts are enabled, otherwise only exactly one or exactly the maximum.

Observed step layout contains a label pointer, single startup and teardown handler pointers with a shared multi handler view, a flag forbidding use as a stable target, a multi instance flag, and a hashed instance list head. Observed per processor state contains numeric current state, desired target and failure injection fields.

Teardown callbacks are assumed never to fail during hotplug transitions and during instance or state removal; failures trigger a fatal check. Removing a multi instance state while instances remain linked only warns and clears the handlers, leaving teardown for those instances unexecuted. Atomic starting and dying stages must not be selected for failure injection or as ad hoc targets without handlers.

Target and failure stores validate numeric ranges before locking, then acquire the device hotplug sysfs guard and briefly take the state mutex only to inspect the target step properties before acting. States listing holds the state mutex for the whole scan. Single processor state reads use per processor access without additional locking shown in these fragments.
Architecture hooks surrounding thawed processor bringup default to weak empty implementations, allowing platforms to override begin and end actions without changing generic thaw logic.
Frozen set uses static storage for a dynamically allocated processor mask pointer, allocated once during early init as zeroed.
Boundary ordering places offline below all installable states and online above them, with an invalid sentinel used to clear failure injection.
